# QA — identify manual-verification scenarios

Keep `qa-manual-verification/` a **complete, deduplicated catalog** of the
product's user-facing flows: one `NNN-{scenario-name}.md` per flow, indexed by
`qa-manual-verification/README.md`. This skill is the first link in the QA chain;
its output is what [[qa-feedback]] logs against and [[qa-address-issues]] later
fixes.

This skill is **incremental and additive**. If scenarios already exist, review
what is there, find what is missing, and add only the gaps. Never duplicate a
flow already covered, and do not renumber existing files.

## Numbering & location (contract)

- Scenarios live at `qa-manual-verification/NNN-{scenario-name}.md`.
- `NNN` is **3-digit, zero-padded** (`000`, `001`, … `030`, …).
- `{scenario-name}` is a short, lowercase, hyphenated slug matching the existing
  style (e.g. `detalle-licitacion`, `equipo-invitaciones-y-roles`).
- `999-qa-feedback.md` is **reserved** for the feedback template — never assign
  `999` to a scenario, and never go past it.
- New scenarios get the **next free number after the highest existing scenario**
  (e.g. if `030` is the max, the next is `031`). Slot them into the right
  thematic section of the README matrix; do not reshuffle existing numbers.

## Step 1 — Discover the product surface (inspect, don't guess)

First **detect the project's actual layout** — list the top-level directories and
read the root README / PRD / package manifest to learn how *this* codebase is
organized. Map real flows from what you find, not from memory or assumption.

The areas below are the usual sources of user-facing flows. The paths in
parentheses are what **this repository** happens to use; **another project may be
laid out completely differently** — a single Next.js app, a Django service, a Go
CLI, a mobile app, a monorepo, microservices, a library, etc. Translate each
bullet to the equivalent location in whatever stack you are actually in:

- **Frontend / UI** — user-facing screens and journeys (here: `web/src/app/**`
  + `components/**`; elsewhere `src/`, `app/`, `pages/`, a mobile target, a TUI,
  or CLI commands). Each coherent journey a user can perform is a candidate
  scenario.
- **Backend / API** — the endpoints/routers/handlers behind those screens, plus
  gating, validation, and auth (here: `api/`; elsewhere `server/`, `services/`,
  `cmd/`, lambda handlers).
- **Background / async work** — jobs, workers, crons, or queues a flow depends on
  (here: `background/`; elsewhere `workers/`, `tasks/`, schedulers).
- **Product intent** — the spec for what *should* exist: PRD, design docs,
  product README, or issue tracker (here: `prd/PRD.md`, `prd/*.md`). Use it to
  find plan gating and feature flags, and to catch flows not yet built.

If a project has no UI (a pure library, SDK, or CLI), map the equivalent
user-facing surface instead — public commands, the API contract, SDK entry
points.

Group by **end-to-end flow** (something a user does), not per-endpoint or
per-file. A flow may span several of the areas above.

## Step 2 — Read what already exists

Read `qa-manual-verification/README.md` (the scope matrix) and the `# NNN —`
titles and scope line (the **Alcance:** field in this repo) of the existing
`NNN-*.md` files. Build the set of flows already covered.

## Step 3 — Diff and report before writing

Produce the full flow list, marking each **existing** or **missing**. Show this
to the user before creating files so they can confirm scope. For flows that
exist but look stale (code drifted from the scenario), note the drift — do not
rewrite an existing scenario unless the user asks.

## Step 4 — Create the missing scenarios

For each missing flow, add `qa-manual-verification/NNN-{scenario-name}.md` using
the **exact format of the existing files**. The template below reflects *this*
repository's convention (Spanish, these sections, the legend in Step 5). **Derive
the real format from the existing `NNN-*.md` files** — their language, section
set, and tone — and match it. If the folder is empty (a fresh project), establish
a clear equivalent in the project's own language and keep every scenario
consistent with it.

```markdown
# NNN — <Título del flujo>

**Alcance:** <qué cubre, con rutas REALES de código
(p. ej. `web/src/app/buscar/page.tsx`, `api/src/app/api/...`, job `official-source`)
y referencia al PRD §X cuando aplique>.
**Estado:** <activo/gated por defecto> (<iconos Requiere>). <prerequisitos>.

## Precondiciones

- Stack levantado (ver `000-setup-entorno.md`).
- <datos/jobs/flags necesarios, p. ej. ingesta hecha con job `official-source`>.

## Pasos

1. <paso concreto y observable, con URL/selector/copy esperado>
2. …

## Resultado esperado

- <qué debe verse / qué garantiza el flujo>
- Email: <aplica (asunto / `template_name`) | no aplica>.

## Variantes / casos límite

- <sin JS, sin sesión, gating, errores, multi-sesión, …>

## Feedback / hallazgos

| # | Severidad | Paso | Esperado | Observado | Ruta/fichero | Notas |
|---|-----------|------|----------|-----------|--------------|-------|
```

Rules for the content:

- Cite **real** paths/jobs/PRD sections — open the files to confirm them; never
  invent a route or component.
- Cross-reference other scenarios by their 3-digit id (e.g. ``ver `000` §4``,
  ``escenario `018-…` ``), matching how existing files link.
- Match the surrounding files' density, tone, language, and section set (Spanish
  in this repo — follow whatever the existing files actually use).

## Step 5 — Register in the README

Add the scenario to the correct section table **and** the scope matrix in
`qa-manual-verification/README.md`, reusing **whatever legend the README already
defines**. In *this* repo that is the "Requiere" legend:

> 🔓 público (sin sesión) · 🔑 sesión · 👥 2+ sesiones (equipo) · 💼 plan Pro ·
> ⚙️ correr un job · 🚩 activar un feature flag.

Another project's README may use different markers (or none) — read it and stay
consistent rather than importing this one. Keep the `#` column 3-digit and
consistent with the filename.

## Guardrails

- Never duplicate a flow already covered; one flow per file.
- Edit only inside `qa-manual-verification/` (scenario files + README). Do not
  touch application code from this skill.
- Do not commit unless the user asks.
